'''Jan Karel Lenstra''' (born 19 December 1947, in [[Zaandam]]) is a Dutch [[mathematician]] and [[operations research]]er, known for his work on scheduling problems, the [[travelling salesman problem]], complexity, approximation, and [[Local search (optimization)|local search]].

Lenstra received his Ph.D. from the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1976, advised by [[Gijsbert de Leve]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Jan Karel Lenstra|id=51371}}.</ref> He then became a researcher at the [[Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica]] (CWI), where he remained until 1989. After taking positions at the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] (where he became Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science) and the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], he returned to CWI as its director in 2003. He stepped down in 2011, and at that time became a CWI Fellow.<ref name="cwi-lion">{{citation|title=Royal Decoration for Former CWI Director Jan Karel Lenstra|date=November 4, 2011|url=http://www.cwi.nl/news/2011/royal-decoration-mathematician-and-former-cwi-director-jan-karel-lenstra|publisher=[[Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica]]}}.</ref><ref name="cwi-profile">[http://www.cwi.nl/people/275 Faculty profile], CWI, retrieved 2026-03-03.</ref> He was editor-in-chief of ''[[Mathematics of Operations Research]]'' from 1993 to 1998, and of ''[[Operations Research Letters]]'' from 2002 to 2021.

Lenstra became an [[INFORMS]] Fellow in 2004.<ref>[http://www.informs.org/Connect-with-People/Fellows/INFORMS-Fellows-Class-of-2004 INFORMS Fellows: Class of 2004] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111206125736/http://informs.org/Connect-with-People/Fellows/INFORMS-Fellows-Class-of-2004 |date=2011-12-06 }}, INFORMS, retrieved 2011-11-08.</ref>
In 1997, he was awarded the [[EURO Gold Medal]], the highest distinction within [[Operations Research]] in Europe.
In 2011, he was made a Knight of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]],<ref name="cwi-lion"/> and the CWI organized a symposium in his honor.<ref>[https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/19475 Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica: Jan Karel Lenstra, the traveling science man : liber amicorum], retrieved 2011-11-08.</ref>

Lenstra was chair of the [[Mathematical Optimization Society]], of the [[Royal Dutch Mathematical Society]], and of advisory committees of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] on mathematics in primary education and on digital literacy in secondary education. He chaired the committees for the [[Spinoza Prize]] and the [[Stevin Prize]] of the Dutch Science Council.

Lenstra is the brother of [[Arjen Lenstra]], Andries Lenstra, and [[Hendrik Lenstra]], all of whom are also mathematicians. His daughter Catrien (1976) is CEO of the City of Amsterdam. He is married to [[Karen Aardal]], who is professor of optimization at [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mensen|url=https://web.tue.nl/cursor/bastiaan/jaargang48/cursor15/rubrieken/m_interview.html|access-date=2021-02-04|website=web.tue.nl}}</ref> They have two children, Lisa (1999) and Jacob (2003).

== Publications ==

* [http://dblp.uni-trier.de/pers/hd/l/Lenstra:Jan_Karel Jan Karel Lenstra] // [[DBLP]], [[University of Trier|Universität Trier]]
* Peter Brucker, Jan Karel Lenstra, [[Alexander Rinnooy Kan|Alexander H.G. Rinnooy Kan]]. Complexity of machine scheduling problems. ''Annals of Discrete Mathematics 1'' (1977), 343–362.
* Ronald L. Graham, [[Eugene Lawler|Eugene L. Lawler]], Jan Karel Lenstra, Alexander H.G. Rinnooy Kan. Optimization and approximation in deterministic sequencing and scheduling; a survey. ''Annals of Discrete Mathematics 5'' (1979), 287–326.
* J. Blazewicz, Jan Karel Lenstra, Alexander H.G. Rinnooy Kan. Scheduling subject to resource constraints; classification and complexity. ''Discrete Applied Mathematics 5'' (1983), 11–24.
* Eugene L. Lawler, Jan Karel Lenstra, Alexander H.G. Rinnooy Kan, [[David Shmoys|David B. Shmoys]] (eds.). ''The traveling salesman problem; a guided tour of combinatorial optimization'', Wiley, Chichester (1985).
* Jan Karel Lenstra, David B. Shmoys, Éva Tardos. Approximation algorithms for scheduling unrelated parallel machines. ''Mathematical Programming 46'' (1990), 259–271.
* Peter J. M. van Laarhoven, Emile H. L. Aarts, Jan Karel Lenstra. - [http://www.cs.amherst.edu/ccm/cs34/papers/jobshop171189.pdf Job Shop Scheduling by Simulated Annealing] ([http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=133767 info]) // [[Operations Research]], {{comment|40 (1992)|Volume 40 Issue 1, Jan.–Feb. 1992}}, pp. 113-125.
* Eugene L. Lawler, Jan Karel Lenstra, Alexander H.G. Rinnooy Kan, David B. Shmoys. Sequencing and scheduling; algorithms and complexity. S.C. Graves, A.H.G. Rinnooy Kan, P. Zipkin (eds.). ''Handbooks in operations research and management science; volume 4; logistics of production and inventory'', North-Holland, Amsterdam (1993), 445–522.
* Emile H. L. Aarts, Peter J. M. van Laarhoven, Jan Karel Lenstra, Nico L. J. Ulder: A Computational Study of Local Search Algorithms for Job Shop Scheduling. // INFORMS Journal on Computing 6(2): 118-125 (1994) ([http://dblp.uni-trier.de/pers/hd/l/Laarhoven:Peter_J=_M=_van dblp])
* Emile H.L. Aarts, Jan Karel Lenstra. ''Local search in combinatorial optimization'', Wiley, Chichester (1997)
* Jan Karel Lenstra, David B. Shmoys. ''elementsofscheduling.nl'' [https://elementsofscheduling.nl/]. (This website presents fragments of an unfinished book on machine scheduling.)
